title: Hyderabad (Batch 2)

overview.text:
Hyderabad, the capital of Telangana, was founded on the Musi River in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah and later became the capital of the Nizams. Their legacy fills the Old City south of the river: Charminar and the bangle stalls of Laad Bazaar, Mecca Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace and the Salar Jung Museum, with the world's largest one-man collection of antiques. On the city's western edge, Golconda Fort tells the older story with an evening light and sound show.

North of the river, Hussain Sagar, dug in 1562, joins Hyderabad to its twin city Secunderabad, with a 16 m monolithic Buddha in the middle. Food is the other great draw: UNESCO lists Hyderabad as a Creative City of Gastronomy, and its biryani and haleem carry GI tags. Visit between October and February to avoid the summer heat.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (HYD) handles domestic and international flights.

By train: Secunderabad is the main station, with Hyderabad Deccan (Nampally), Kacheguda and Lingampalli for some trains.

By road: Hyderabad is about 570 km from Bengaluru, 699 km from Mumbai and 1,566 km from Delhi.

local_transport.text: The Hyderabad Metro, open since November 2017, links Secunderabad, the centre and the HITEC City area. For the Old City and Golconda, use autos, app cabs or a hired car. Laad Bazaar and the lanes around Charminar are best explored on foot.

best_time.text: October to February is the most comfortable time, with December–January lows occasionally near 10 °C. Summer (March–June) is hot and dry, often above 40 °C from April to June. The monsoon brings heavy rain from June to October. During Ramadan, the Old City's bazaars are at their liveliest in the evenings, and Eid, Diwali, Ugadi and Bonalu are all celebrated with enthusiasm.

items.body: Biryani, haleem and Old City sweets in a UNESCO city of gastronomy.

items.title: History lovers
items.body: Charminar, Golconda, Chowmahalla Palace and the Salar Jung Museum.

items.body: Hussain Sagar's boats and Buddha statue, and Ramoji Film City.
Bangles, jewellery and fabrics in Laad Bazaar by Charminar.
Pearls: Hyderabad is the City of Pearls, with drilling centred on Chandanpet.
The Pearl Market and Madina Circle in the Old City.
Visiting in April–June without planning for heat above 40 °C. Do sights early and late.

Eating only biryani. Try haleem, mirchi ka salan and double ka meetha too.

items.title: What is Hyderabad famous for?
items.body: Charminar, Golconda Fort, the Nizams' palaces, pearls, and its food: biryani and haleem carry GI tags.

items.title: When is the best time to visit?
items.body: October to February. Summers are very hot and June–October is the monsoon.

items.title: Which railway station should I use?
items.body: Secunderabad is the main station; check whether your train stops at Hyderabad Deccan or Kacheguda instead.

items.title: How many days do I need?
items.body: Two days covers the Old City, Golconda and Hussain Sagar.

In Ramadan: return to Laad Bazaar in the evening, when it is at its busiest.

faqs.q: Can I see Golconda and Charminar on the same day?
faqs.a: It's possible but rushed. Golconda is best in the late afternoon, with the evening show.
Biryani and haleem (both GI-tagged), mirchi ka salan, double ka meetha and qubani ka meetha.

faqs.q: Is Laad Bazaar safe to walk?
faqs.a: It's busy and best explored on foot. Keep valuables secure in the crowds.
